corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN, in line with R4. As a statement about every one-hidden-layer network at general s = nu/b, I found no prior proof of prop:coverage. Two things are already in the literature. First, the normalisation template (homogeneity -> Fourier-domain l_{b/nu} quasi-norm budget -> margin <= max-margin on the unit quasi-norm ball x quasi-norm) is Gunasekar et al. NeurIPS 2018, Thm 2a + Lemma 7, for linear conv nets with b=2, nu=L. Second, the s=1 instance for idealised Fourier logits is Kam et al. 2026, App. A.3.2, Eq. (18): Delta_S(beta) <= p/(p-1) sum_k beta_k. prop:coverage is a one-line rescaling and no novelty claim should rest on it.
issues:
1) MISSED PRIOR ART (template): Gunasekar, Lee, Soudry, Srebro, NeurIPS 2018 (vol. 31; arXiv 1806.00468). I read the PDF.
- Thm 2a: the GD limit is "a scaling of a first order stationary point of min ||beta^||_{2/L} s.t. forall n, y_n<beta,x_n> >= 1" (eq. 10), where beta^ are the DFT coefficients. The paper notes 2/L < 1 gives a non-convex quasi-norm.
- Lemma 7: min ||w||_2^2 = L ||beta^||_{2/L}^{2/L}.
- This is the same homogeneity -> Fourier quasi-norm -> max-margin-over-quasi-norm-ball reduction, with b=2, nu=L. prop:coverage is its nonlinear, Z_p-coverage analogue: exact for linear predictors there, while ours goes through the phase lemma plus subadditivity.
- The R4 checker found this paper; the R5 checker did not cross-reference it. The R5 verdict should match R4's PARTIALLY_KNOWN.

2) KAM ET AL. (arXiv 2609.17926) IS MISCHARACTERISED. I verified title, authors, 15 Sep 2026 and "Under review at NeurReps 2026" on the abs page; the bib is fine. From the v1 PDF, App. A.3.2:
- Eq. (15), Delta_S(beta) = min_{s!=0} sum_k beta_k(1-cos(omega_k s)), is the separation of the IDEALISED Fourier-logit solution. It is not an upper bound on any network's margin.
- The budget ||beta||_2 = B is exogenous, not derived from homogeneity.
- The proof of Prop. 5 (Eq. 18) literally contains Delta_S(beta) <= p/(p-1) sum_k beta_k. That is the s=1 case of prop:coverage, with Gamma_1 = p/(p-1), matching cor:dense, and uses the same averaging identity. l2 enters only afterwards, via Cauchy-Schwarz.
- Uniform allocation is optimal only at full frequency content. For proper subsets, Nelder-Mead beats uniform by 25% (K=4) and 28% (K=10).
- The authors explicitly disclaim the budget account ("gives no support to the budget account and we do not claim it does"; "we record its absence rather than presenting the calculation ... as an explanation").
- Fixes: the checker's "margin <= return x budget ... with exponent 2" is loose. The suggested sentence "where the optimum is dense" should read "where at full frequency content the uniform allocation is optimal (their Prop. 5)".

3) MORWANI (arXiv 2311.07568): confirmed. v2 comments say "Accepted as Spotlight at ICLR 2024", and iclr.cc/virtual/2024/poster/18073 lists it as a Spotlight Poster. The refs.bib entry is correct.
- Sec. 4 = cyclic groups. The phase condition theta_u+theta_v=theta_w is Thm 7(1).
- eta_{u,v,w}(delta) is defined in App. F.1, not the main text, averaged uniformly over delta != 0 (eq. 4). AM-GM is eq. 9.
- There is no worst-offset coverage bound and no general-s budget. The paper could point to "App. F.1" when it cites eta_{u,v,w}.

4) OTHER PAPERS CHECKED. Full-text greps (margin, 1-cos, budget, quasi-norm) found no bound of this form in: Li et al. 2402.09469, McCracken 2505.18266 (unnormalised unit-amplitude coverage, sufficiency only), He et al. 2602.16849 (Rem. 5.1 average margin), Huang-Li 2511.23443 (single construction), Mohamadi 2407.12332, Tian 2410.01779, Tan-Gai-Zhang 2606.08985 and 2606.05863. I also screened the 40 S2 citers of Morwani.

5) SEARCH LIMITS. The WebSearch budget was exhausted, and Semantic Scholar keyword/snippet search returned 429. I used the arXiv API, the S2 citation list, OpenAlex and full-text PDFs instead.

extra_citations.why: Thm 2a and Lemma 7 (arXiv 1806.00468, read in full): homogeneity turns the l2 weight cost into an l_{2/L} quasi-norm on Fourier coefficients (min ||w||^2 = L||beta^||_{2/L}^{2/L}), and the margin is maximised over that quasi-norm ball. prop:coverage is the same normalisation template with b=2, nu=L; ours extends it to nonlinear one-hidden-layer nets on Z_p via the phase lemma. Cite at eq:programme / prop:coverage, as R4 already recommends.
